newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WAUGH SAYS ENGLISH CRICKETERS WEAK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WAUGH SAYS ENGLISH CRICKETERS WEAK.

text.p: Australia batsman Mark Waugh has criticised England cricketers for being self-centred and lacking the toughness to become a force in test cricket.
In comments likely to inflame old rivalries in the upcoming Ashes tour, Waugh predicted Australia would exploit those weaknesses to record an easy win in the six test series.

"I look at the (England) team on paper and think they are good players, but they aren't tough enough or hungry enough on the field," said Waugh in an interview with an Australian Broadcasting Corporation magazine to be published on Wednesday.
"They don't play as a team, they worry about themselves. When you're out there, you don't feel you've got 11 guys against you," said Australia's stylish number four batsman.
"They (England) just haven't got the toughness you need to win test cricket consistently. Man for man they are not that far behind us, but they lack hunger," Waugh said.
Waugh said Australia will capture the Ashes in the northern hemisphere summer even if hosts England improve and the tourists play below their best.
"I think it (the result) will be similar to 1993 and that was 4-1. If England lift and if we play below our best, perhaps 3-2 to Australia," Waugh said in the tour preview publication.
Waugh, a veteran of 63 tests, said England lacked a quality spinner in their bowling attack, dismissing Phil Tufnell as a threat.
"I don't think there is a quality spinner in their side. Off spinner Robert Croft is probably the best -- I rate him highly.
"Phil Tufnell is back in the fray but I don't see him as a danger. I see him as a fairly weak sort of player who relies on you to make a mistake. He's not going to get you out."
But Waugh praised England fast bowler Darren Gough for his attitude and skill.
"He's always trying 100 percent, having a go, trying a bumper, a slower ball. If he starts bowling well, he's a dangerous man because he can lift the rest of the team."
Australia's 17-man squad will leave for England in May in preparation for the first test at Edgbaston in Birmingham in early June.
